Dan Sullivan loses elections The Justice Department asked a federal court to bar Alaska from certifying the Nov. 3 Senate result if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses and votes for a second candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan could have changed the outcome. President Trump said he ordered the suit.

Supreme Court lets New Hampshire bar student IDs as backup voter ID for midterms courts The Supreme Court on Thursday granted New Hampshire's emergency request and paused a lower-court order, allowing the state to bar student IDs as a backup way for voters to prove their identity in the Nov. 3 election.

OpenAI opens its Decisions API to all developers

OpenAI made its Decisions API generally available on Thursday, a service that answers bounded questions (a yes/no probability, a pick from a fixed list, or a rubric score) instead of generating free text. It runs on GPT-6 Luna and costs $0.10 per million input tokens ($0.01 cached), with no charge for output tokens. Since its public beta, OpenAI added GPT-Live voice integration, image and JSON inputs, US and EU processing, and a limit of 400 questions per request.

Why it matters: Apps and AI agents make many small routing and classification calls, and running each through a full chat model adds delay. OpenAI now offers a separate endpoint for these calls. Early users included Box, Datadog, Ramp and Speak, and Speak says its time between actions fell from 1.4 seconds to 0.13 seconds in its own testing. These speed figures come from OpenAI and its customers, not independent tests.

FAA proposes inspecting overhead bins on 1,370 U.S. Airbus A320-family jets

The FAA said bushings, retainer rings and pins at the bins' attachment points had migrated on several in-service aircraft, and that left unaddressed the problem could weaken the bins under emergency landing loads, according to the proposed rule. A bin that detaches could injure occupants, the agency said. The proposal follows a European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) directive issued in November 2025.

The FAA estimates the rule would cover 1,370 U.S.-registered planes, with an inspection of up to five work-hours, or $425, per aircraft, Aviation Shop reported. Comments are due by December 21, 2026.
